text:
one of my ai benchmarks has been if the models / harnesses can automated grocery ordering for me

@bot is the first one to solve this well, what it gets right:

- a dedicated chat for groceries where i can state preferences i.e "no olives" and it remembers them over time
- a browser it can use and i can sign into amazon & costo on 
- automated tasks to run ordering on a schedule
- access to my MCPs (shoutout executor) so it can update my calendar with what to cook and when
- having an actual running machine to take over and sign in to sites is so nice

what it's missing is collaboration, i.e i want to include my girlfriend on this chat 

an artifacts system would also be nice, although i can just use executor for that but i need to expand it with storage for mini apps

also the way that it uses the browser is very slow - i would've liked to see it have some form of claude workflows style approach where it can parallelize work 

not as big of a deal as this'll be a mainly background job, but i think codex's chrome plugin still wins out

what's maybe most interesting here is how it replaces something like a HelloFresh for me, it's a significantly better experience, cheaper, and i can be more granular with my preferences over time

with the fact that it's doing work in the background, if i really wanted i could:
- order bulk goods / frozen meat from costco
- order fresh produce from whole foods
- order misc items from amazon fresh

obviously wouldn't want to do that on every order, but it can better order the right items from places whereas i previously wouldn't care to

the last thing is on the computer, i'm really wanting a cloud browser that i can connect to my agents over MCP

as i get more bots i don't want to have to reauth to each one, same thing with the CLIs that'd be installed on the machines

i basically want my browser but running in the cloud, which can be forked or spawned with specific credentials

browserbase / kernel may be the answer to that part, but my understanding on them is they're more
